transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because things have been happening for months, and people keep acting like it’s nothing. My husband’s family has been quietly interfering with our money and how people see us. Little billing mistakes show up at work, or someone at church acts strange toward me, and everyone says the records don’t show anything. But I know it connects back to them.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No… I don’t think so. Not voices when nobody’s there.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or unusually irritable?
I don’t know… I mean, I get upset, sure, but unusually high? No, I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Have you felt as if someone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?
No… I don’t think anything like that. My thoughts feel like mine. I just… I haven’t noticed someone putting them there or taking them away.
Do you ever hear voices talking about you or commenting on what you’re doing?
No… not voices talking about me. I haven’t noticed that.
Have these beliefs about your husband’s family interfering been present for at least three months?
Yes… it’s been more than three months. Maybe around nine months now, since things started with his family about the money and the holidays.
Compared with before this started, have you had a big drop in how well you manage your work or daily responsibilities?

Not really a big drop, no. I still get up and go to work, do my billing stuff, keep the house going. I garden some, paint when I can. It’s mostly… the problems happen when I try to tell people what his family is doing.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t felt like people could hear my thoughts or anything like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory belief that her husband's family is interfering with finances and social reputation for approximately nine months. She denies hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, thought broadcasting, and mood episodes, and there is no marked deterioration in overall functioning outside the impact of the delusional belief. This pattern is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
